First identified in cyclin-F as a protein-protein interaction motif, the F-box is a conserved domain that is present in numerous proteins with a bipartite structure [[cite:PUB00000938]]. Through the F-box, these proteins are linked to the Skp1 protein and the core of SCFs (Skp1-cullin-F-box protein ligase) complexes. SCFs complexes constitute a new class of E3 ligases [[cite:PUB00000952]]. They function in combination with the E2 enzyme Cdc34 to ubiquitinate G1 cyclins, Cdk inhibitors and many other proteins, to mark them for degradation. The binding of the specific substrates by SCFs complexes is mediated by divergent protein-protein interaction motifs present in F-box proteins, like WD40 repeats, leucine rich repeats [[cite:PUB00018180], [cite:PUB00018181]] or ANK repeats.

This entry identifies a domain superfamily containing adjacent WD repeats. These WD repeats are located on β-sheets (blades) that fold into a higher order structure called β-propeller. WD-40 repeats (also known as WD or β-transducin repeats) are short ~40 amino acid motifs, often terminating in a Trp-Asp (W-D) dipeptide. WD40 repeats usually assume a 7-8 bladed β-propeller fold, but proteins have been found with 4 to 16 repeated units, which also form a circularised β-propeller structure. WD-repeat proteins are a large family found in all eukaryotes and are implicated in a variety of functions ranging from signal transduction and transcription regulation to cell cycle control and apoptosis. Repeated WD40 motifs act as a site for protein-protein or protein-DNA interaction, and proteins containing WD40 repeats are known to serve as platforms for the assembly of protein complexes or mediators of transient interplay among other proteins [[cite:PUB00094364]]. The specificity of the proteins is determined by the sequences outside the repeats themselves. Examples of such complexes are G proteins (beta subunit is a β-propeller), TAFII transcription factor, and E3 ubiquitin ligase [[cite:PUB00015237], [cite:PUB00005491]]. In Arabidopsis spp., several WD40-containing proteins act as key regulators of plant-specific developmental events.

This superfamily represents a WD40/YVTN repeat-like domain. Both the WD40 and the YVTN repeated motifs consist of about 40 residues, and although they consist of distinct sequences, they do share a similar structure. Structurally, both the WD40 and the YVTN repeated motifs form seven-bladed propellers (although some members can contain eight blades), which consist of seven 4-stranded β-sheets.

This entry represents a β-propeller found at the N-terminal end of IFT122 and at the C-terminal of SMU1. Members of this group are found in eukaryotes and bacteria. Intraflagellar transport protein 122 homolog (IFT122) is one of the core components (together with WDR19/IFT144 and IFT140) of the IFT-A complex which is required for retrograde ciliary transport and entry into cilia of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), being involved in cilia function and/or assembly [[cite:PUB00155528], [cite:PUB00101516]]. IFT-A polymerises interacts with IFT-B, and uses an array of β-propeller and TPR domains to create 'carriages' of the IFT train that engage TULP adaptor proteins [[cite:PUB00101516]]. Human WD40 repeat-containing protein SMU1 is involved in pre-mRNA splicing as a component of the spliceosome [[cite:PUB00090272]], and is required for normal accumulation of IK [[cite:PUB00162459]].
